boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct, officially documented UGA Libraries study environments across the Main Library, Miller Learning Center, and McBay Science Library.

cards.title: Graduate Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Main Library, third floor
cards.notes: Set up at a table overlooking the quad, and keep this silent-study designation in mind when choosing solo reading or focused writing.
cards.short_summary: A silent third-floor room with a view of the Main Library quad.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA Libraries designates the third-floor Graduate Reading Room as a silent study area; it is open to all and overlooks the quad.
cards.access_notes: Main Library study spaces are limited after 6 p.m. to the UGA community and students with valid college ID.

cards.title: Collaborative Study Space
cards.subtitle: Main Library, fourth floor
cards.notes: Bring a discussion outline and use the whiteboard walls or chalkboard columns to map ideas; a WEPA print kiosk is also in the space.
cards.short_summary: A fourth-floor group workspace built around writable surfaces.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA Libraries says the Main Library's fourth-floor Collaborative Study Space has seating for groups, whiteboard walls, chalkboard columns, and a WEPA print kiosk.
cards.access_notes: Main Library study spaces are limited after 6 p.m. to the UGA community and students with valid college ID.

cards.title: Window Nooks
cards.subtitle: Main Library, rear of floors 2–7
cards.notes: Choose a small or large rear-window table for a solo task or a compact work session, with a campus-facing view beside your materials.
cards.short_summary: Rear-window tables spread across the Main Library's upper floors.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA Libraries identifies Window Nooks at the rear of Main Library floors 2–7, with small and large tables and views of campus.
cards.access_notes: Main Library study spaces are limited after 6 p.m. to the UGA community and students with valid college ID.

cards.title: Study Carrels
cards.subtitle: Main Library, floors 3–6
cards.notes: Use an available carrel for private, individual work; only a small number are first-come, first-served, while some are long-term reserved.
cards.short_summary: Enclosed individual study stations on Main Library floors three through six.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA Libraries lists individual Main Library study carrels on floors 3–6; a small number are first-come, first-served, while eligible faculty and graduate students may reserve long-term carrels.
cards.access_notes: For UGA affiliates; access to Main Library study spaces is limited after 6 p.m. to the UGA community and students with valid college ID.

cards.title: MAGIL Open Study Spaces
cards.subtitle: Map & Government Information Library, Main Library sub-basement
cards.notes: Head to the sub-basement for a quieter table or individual space, particularly when working with map and government information library materials.
cards.short_summary: Quiet tables and individual spaces in the Main Library's map collection.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA Libraries states that the Map & Government Information Library in the Main Library sub-basement provides tables and individual spaces for quiet study or using library materials.
cards.access_notes: Main Library study spaces are limited after 6 p.m. to the UGA community and students with valid college ID.

cards.title: Sidney Samuel Thomas Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Miller Learning Center, third floor
cards.notes: Use this quiet room for concentrated reading, and plan around its posted maximum capacity of 100; the small book collection does not circulate.
cards.short_summary: A quiet MLC reading room with seating capped at 100.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA Libraries describes the Sidney Samuel Thomas Reading Room on MLC's third floor as a quiet study space with a maximum capacity of 100 and a small non-circulating collection.
cards.access_notes: MLC study spaces are limited after 9 p.m. to the UGA community and students with valid college ID.

cards.title: MLC Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Miller Learning Center, floors 2–4
cards.notes: Bring at least one collaborator, then use the room locator or floor displays to find an opening; rooms have whiteboards and are first-come, first-served.
cards.short_summary: First-come group rooms with whiteboards throughout the MLC.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA Libraries says 95 group study rooms on MLC floors 2–4 are first-come, first-served, and the rooms have whiteboards; the UGA App can show availability.
cards.access_notes: MLC study spaces are limited after 9 p.m. to the UGA community and students with valid college ID. Group rooms prioritize groups.

cards.title: Study Spaces with Workstations
cards.subtitle: Miller Learning Center, floors 3 Central, 3 East, and 4 East
cards.notes: Choose one of the individual workstation seats when you need a campus computer, locating the designated areas on MLC's third and fourth floors.
cards.short_summary: More than 200 individual MLC seats equipped with computer workstations.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA Libraries reports that the MLC has over 200 individual study spaces with computer workstations on floors 3 Central, 3 East, and 4 East.
cards.access_notes: MLC study spaces are limited after 9 p.m. to the UGA community and students with valid college ID.

cards.title: Study Booths
cards.subtitle: McBay Science Library, second floor
cards.notes: Use the booth seating for a paired discussion or a reading session, choosing this second-floor wing when you want a more contained setup.
cards.short_summary: Booth seating in a dedicated McBay Science Library wing.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA Libraries identifies a wing of study booths on McBay Science Library's second floor, with seating for study and discussion.
cards.access_notes: McBay Science Library study spaces are limited after 6 p.m. to the UGA community and students with valid college ID.

cards.title: McBay Fourth-Floor Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: McBay Science Library, fourth floor
cards.notes: Check availability in the UGA App before meeting up, then use one of the 25 small group rooms for shared problem-solving or planning.
cards.short_summary: Twenty-five small group rooms on McBay's renovated fourth floor.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA Libraries states that McBay Science Library's fourth floor has 25 small group study rooms, with availability available through the UGA App.
cards.access_notes: McBay Science Library study spaces are limited after 6 p.m. to the UGA community and students with valid college ID.
